When N ≤ T 1−ǫ we may evaluate M1 (R, T ) and M2 (R, T ) easily. These are two quadratic
forms in the unknown coefficients r(n), and the problem thus reduces to maximizing the
ratio of these quadratic forms. Solving this optimization problem we obtain Theorem 1.
   This method generalizes readily to provide large and small central values in families of
L-functions. By contrast, the method of Montgomery does not appear to generalize to this
situation. Recently Z. Rudnick and the author ([11] and [12]) found a flexible method to
obtain lower bounds for moments in many families of L-functions, but the bounds obtained
here are superior.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The same resonance perspective is made two-sided in a quadratic-character family: coefficient alignment can select exceptionally large central values or exceptionally small ones.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The theorem states the existence, among fundamental discriminants of size X, of both a large central quadratic Dirichlet L-value and a very small one, and notes that many small values can also be obtained.
directed.conceptual_reading: Extremality is controlled by the sign of correlation rather than by a method dedicated only to growth; small nonzero values remain a distinct phenomenon from forced vanishing or unresolved positivity.
directed.representation_or_bridge: A family indexed by discriminants replaces continuous t-averaging, allowing a character-valued resonator to compare a norm average with a central-value-weighted average.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The theorem does not settle Chowla's positivity conjecture or turn smallness into vanishing; the later proof's restriction to discriminants 8d is only an existence subfamily.
directed.uncertainty: The large/small conclusions are clear, but exact exponential constants, fractions, and the quantitative frequency claim are formula-sensitive.

supported: The span states separate existence results for a large central quadratic Dirichlet value and a value with very small absolute magnitude among fundamental discriminants of size X.
It discusses Chowla's positivity conjecture, known nonvanishing and positivity proportions, and a frequency claim for small values.
inference: Treating large and small values as two extremal directions is reasonable, but the mechanism selecting those directions is not supplied in this span.
unsupported_or_imported: The candidate calls the theorem's small value 'small nonzero'; the displayed upper bound on absolute value does not certify that the selected value is nonzero.
The character-valued resonator, its family moments, and control by the sign of correlation belong to the later proof and are absent from this exact span and bounded nearby context.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Hecke multiplication and Petersson averaging yield a gcd kernel
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Combines the approximate functional equation with Hecke relations and Petersson orthogonality to reduce the central-value-weighted resonator average to a finite quadratic form with kernel sigma of the gcd divided by the geometric mean.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The same prime-supported magnitude profile can select large or small central values because a Mobius sign twist reverses the linear prime contributions in the mixed-moment Euler product while leaving the norm essentially unchanged.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: This paired sign mechanism is demonstrated for the quadratic-character and cusp-form families; the zeta section proves large values only.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The final optimization reuses the same sparse multiplicative magnitudes across families: positive coefficients reinforce the gcd-kernel interaction for large values, while Möbius twisting reverses the linear local terms for small values.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: With N chosen proportional to k, Rankin's trick evaluates both the resonator norm and the central-value-weighted gcd-kernel form as Euler products. Taking r=f gives positive linear prime contributions and the large-value conclusion of Theorem 3; taking r=μf gives the small-value conclusion.
directed.conceptual_reading: The reusable component is a local coefficient profile, while the sign pattern selects which spectral tail is amplified; family-specific trace machinery only changes the kernel through which that profile acts.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Euler factorization translates the gcd quadratic form into primewise gains, making the Möbius sign switch a direct bridge between coefficient phase and global extremal direction.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The conclusion inherits the harmonic weighting, shortness conditions, and earlier approximate-functional-equation and trace estimates; exact products and constants are not safe from this extraction alone.
directed.uncertainty: The sign-switch mechanism and theorem direction are clear, but product factors, constants, and the exact N choice require PDF verification.

supported: The span chooses N proportional to k and reuses the multiplicative f from the earlier finite optimization.
Rankin's trick gives Euler-product asymptotics for the resonator norm and the central-value-weighted form; the displayed r=f product has positive linear terms and yields large values.
The source then prescribes r=mu f for the small-value conclusion.
inference: The Möbius choice reverses the primewise linear contribution while preserving coefficient magnitudes; this is recoverable from the displayed product and the final instruction, although the small-value product is not displayed.
The sign pattern selecting extremal direction is a sound source-local conceptual reading.
unsupported_or_imported: The statement that family-specific trace machinery 'only changes the kernel' is an unsupported cross-family exclusivity claim; the source also changes weights, length restrictions, and analytic inputs, and this span does not establish an abstract comparison theorem.
context_or_ocr_risk: Exact products, constants, and the admissible N choice require PDF verification.
